static_traits.name: Wang Lei
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate (about to start college)
static_traits.family_status: Living with parents and siblings; strong family support
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships: Good relationship with family, but feeling distant due to worries about college; Social support: family supportive but may not yet fully understand their Fear
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; never received psychotherapy or counseling; without significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe worries and worst-case scenarios concretely; thinking leans toward catastrophizing and predicting the future; active mind at night prone to rumination; Good cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed and Anxiety about starting college soon, worrying about homesickness and eventually dropping out.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because Fear and Anxiety about college have already affected my daily life and sleep patterns.
growth_experiences: Growing up relatively sheltered (sheltered life), Living with parents and siblings, long dependent on family support and familiar routines, never lived far from home or independently for long.
Good academic performance in High school, successful experiences mainly relying on family and friends' support and stable daily routines, feeling safer in familiar environments.

Joined the drama club in High school: initially very nervous, worrying about not fitting in, but eventually made friends and had positive experiences, showing the ability to adapt and build relationships in new groups.

core_beliefs: I am not suited for college life
I am unable to cope and adapt after leaving my family

special_situations.event: At night, when alone, thinks about leaving home soon to go to university
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel strongly homesick at college with Low mood, it means I am unable to adapt and will eventually fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Confides worries to family and friends to seek comfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be homesick, unable to concentrate, and finally drop out

special_situations.event: Imagining the worst scenario of crying alone in the dorm, unable to focus on Learning
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Without familiar support and fixed routines, I am unable to study and live normally
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly rehearsing worst-case scenarios to try to mentally prepare in advance (but actually worsening Anxiety)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be completely isolated, cannot hold on any longer, and finally give up my studies

special_situations.event: When considering building support and routine by joining clubs or using campus resources
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot quickly fit into the group, I will feel even more Loneliness, showing I am not suited for college
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hesitates and delays action; tends to avoid trying
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may not fit in, and will only feel more Loneliness in the end

special_situations.event: After recalling the successful High school drama club experience, seeing college as a 'bigger, scarier' different environment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The new environment is more complex than the past, so past successes have no reference value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating past positive experiences to maintain current vigilance and worry
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That time does not represent now; college is different, I will still fail

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be continuously supported and cared for by family, maintaining familiar connection and safety
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being isolated after leaving home independently, being unable to adapt and failing, not getting support
defense_goal: Lowering Anxiety through Withdrawal and avoiding unfamiliar environments
Maintains close connection with family to gain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable self not suited for college, easily isolated
object_relations.object_representation: The college environment and others seen as unfamiliar, huge, and possibly unsupportive groups

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests taking concrete action (such as looking into campus resources, joining clubs) or discusses leaving home and adjusting to university
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to understand the new environment as unsupportive and isolating, believing attempts will only make them feel more Loneliness
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tending to depict worst-case scenarios, worried tone, emphasizing worries about 'not fitting in', avoiding committing to specific actions.

manifestations: Worrying about not fitting in and feeling more Loneliness
Imagining crying alone in the dorm, unable to focus on Learning
outcomes: Subjectively feeling distant in family relationships

manifestations: The transition from a sheltered life to college life requiring autonomy and self-responsibility triggers unease
Fearing being unable to cope with independence and the new environment
outcomes: Self-doubt ('I am not suited for college life')

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently expressing 'I am not suited for college life'
Overly cautious and self-limiting about integrating into the community

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming the college environment is 'not as supportive as High school'
Worrying that 'others will not accept me/I will not fit in' and inferring the future from it

exception_events.target_problem: When facing new groups and activities, the client usually imagines the worst case, worries about not adapting, and hesitates.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the High school drama club experience, although initially very nervous and worried about not fitting in, he still joined and eventually made friends, gaining a positive experience.
exception_events.reason: Different support and approach: actively trying new activities and engaging peers at the time, gaining group support and belonging, reducing worries about not adapting.

positive_force: The family as a whole is fairly supportive
Good High school academic performance, possessing Learning ability and discipline
Once successfully adapted to a new group in the drama club, possessing resources to build relationships and adapt to new environments
Motivated to seek help and change (proactively seeks counseling)
negative_force: Catastrophizing, predicting the future, Overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking
Fear of separation and the Unknown, over-relying on familiar support and fixed routines
Nighttime rumination leads to Sleep disturbed, further worsening daytime functional impairment
Self-doubt and underestimating one's adaptability ('I am not suited for college life')

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic worry about starting college and nighttime insomnia
antecedent: As the start of university approaches
Thinking about leaving family and familiar life
target_behavior.core_reason: Long sheltered life, Fear of the unfamiliar and separation; the inner 'I am not suited for college' core belief and catastrophic/future-predicting cognitive biases jointly drive rumination and Anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping the Anxiety brought by uncertainty and separation, maintaining a sense of security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep patterns disrupted, Decreased appetite, Impaired daytime attention and functioning, increased subjective sense of distance from family
